wire_registry_binding: HistoryReleaseAttestation.verifier_profile_id is ak.history_release_predicates.v1. The enclosing HistoryKeyResponseRecord.service_proof covers the complete attestation. An unsupported verifier profile is rejected only for the affected object and is never translated to an authorization failure.
trust_model: The first durable enqueue is linearized by an honest release service. Its service proof authenticates a closed T1 decision receipt and exact locator/digest vector; the vector is not a portable multi-authority proof. A malicious or stale release service is outside v1's cryptographic guarantee. A future adversarial-service profile requires a separately registered notary/quorum design.

receipt-bound HistoryGovernanceTraversalIntent with exact bootstrap base/current/target SealBasis antichains
the complete retained target-to-base accepted Seal cut, base Seal bodies, delta Control Moves, AvailabilityReceipts, signer-resolution evidence and semantic dependencies
requester current authorization incarnation and replay-derived winning join/reactivation transition
the scope's current monotone history_access value at target
manifest descriptor exact continuous ranges and their canonical union
closed_predicates: require traversal intent trusted_history_base_basis equal the request-signed predecessor-free bootstrap basis and target_basis dominate trusted_current_basis

reverse-walk every target predecessor until exact base leaves, include each interval predecessor or exact base leaf, consume every base leaf, include base Seal bodies and deltas but stop before base predecessors

topologically verify every Seal against predecessor-state frozen notary descriptors, every AvailabilityReceipt and signer/semantic dependency, then apply every delta Control Move with the Realm's frozen compiled profile
derive the current requester membership incarnation, winning join/reactivation transition, every winning MLS epoch transition, ciphersuite and content_scheme exclusively from replayed state
require every descriptor range be a subset of canonical request ranges

read the current monotone history_access cell only: since_join requires every epoch >= the replay-derived current incarnation join_epoch; all_history_for_current_members ignores that floor but still requires the current incarnation
require every transition to be the reducer-effective winning cell value; conflict recovery, Bottom and continuity are reconstructed by normal replay rather than a separate activation witness
require exporter content_scheme in the winning value; standard MLS is ineligible for history delivery
manifest_t0_registry.failure_rule: Any missing, extra, stale, Bottom, mismatched, unauthorized or unavailable input rejects the whole manifest before sequence allocation, response record, admission row or attestation write. Partial range admission is forbidden.

recipient exact current membership incarnation is active
member source exact current membership incarnation is active
Realm is readable and not tombstoned
exact current Circle-owned history_access is evaluated without parent history_access inheritance or cap
recipient and member source have active exact Circle membership incarnations

Circle and parent Realm are readable and not tombstoned

seal_view_locator_rule.basis: Each scope slot carries the complete canonical accepted non-quarantined seal_basis antichain. Selecting one accepted Seal leaf is forbidden, including open_set.
seal_view_locator_rule.projection: RealmCurrentGateProjection and CircleCurrentGateProjection are the only closed projection shapes. They contain current monotone history_access, exact recipient/source authorization incarnation when the registered branch requires it, tombstone facts, and for Circle the parent-Realm intersection plus membership_reconcile_required=false.
seal_view_locator_rule.cas: The first durable chunk-enqueue transaction re-resolves the exact basis, rejects any known successor, recomputes every projection field and digest, and CAS-compares the complete basis+projection before writing anything.

Neither leaf fact is claimed as a service CBA proof or directory lookup.

closed_predicates: one chunk covers one byte-identical archive authorization tuple
every epoch in released_range has an exact archive Event whose historical tuple and transition provenance match

each archive tuple binds accepted_key_evidence_ref and distinct holder_trusted_basis; retained direct Seal traversal proves the effective registered/rotated key tuple from that complete holder basis to the archive target without a singular activation Seal

source_local_only: holder-private blocklists or local UI policy; these are never asserted by the service attestation

linearization: Before the local enqueue transaction the service obtains intent-bound short-lived observations from each required local authority, verifies the source relay and scope facts, then atomically verifies every observation is unexpired. For every Realm/Circle/PCR Seal authority it re-resolves the complete canonical accepted non-quarantined Seal antichain, requires no known successor, recomputes the closed current-gate projection, and CAS-binds the exact basis+projection vector. It then stores the immutable response record and ReleaseAttestation, assigns the request response-stream sequence/cursor, freezes the compact HistoryKeyResponseSendReceipt and charges quota. It does not claim a cross-service atomic snapshot. Failure writes nothing. Exact source retry returns the original byte-identical compact send receipt through request expiry. Recipient high-water ack atomically removes the large response record and attestation; they are not readable after ack.
release_service_binding_rule: The request receipt's frozen release_id is the only release authority for that request. Before first enqueue it must verify that the requester delivery binding still names this same service DID. A ServiceResolution successor for the same service DID is permitted and becomes the current route; rebinding to another service DID rejects first enqueue and requires a new request. v1 does not migrate a mailbox or idempotency ledger. Already accepted records remain byte-identically retryable from the old ledger until expiry.
audit_record: The immutable service-signed ReleaseAttestation created in the first durable chunk-enqueue transaction is the sole history-release audit record. v1 has no history_release_audit policy facet, pre-release audit token, audit evidence carrier or audit authority slot. Compliance projections index attestations; separate approval workflows are orthogonal capabilities.
predicate_failure: Any required locator, authority response, subject, incarnation, tuple, digest or exact binding that is missing, Bottom, stale, mismatched or unavailable rejects the chunk before enqueue. No caller-supplied boolean can replace a predicate.
